prompts.source:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: Dino Atlas ecosystem gallery scene for ages 5–14
Primary request: Create a brand-new evidence-conscious Late Triassic Ischigualasto ecosystem reconstruction centered on a natural eroded bankface and an old exposed volcanic-ash-derived bentonite ribbon, with exactly two living dinosaurs and no interaction claim.

Input images and roles:
Image 1: Eoraptor lunensis body-proportion and color-identity reference only.
Image 2: Eoraptor hand-structure reference only.
Image 3: Chromogisaurus novasi project identity and postcranial proportion reference only.
Image 4: Chromogisaurus preserved-region hindlimb and tail structure reference only.
Do not copy any reference pose, background, camera, lighting, vegetation, or composition. Do not collage or directly reproduce reference pixels.

Scene/backdrop: Cancha de Bochas Member-inspired fluvial-overbank exposure in the Ischigualasto Formation. A natural weathered bankface occupies the left and central 60 percent of the image. A thin pale gray old bentonite/altered-ash ribbon runs almost horizontally across the middle of the bank and is interrupted once by a narrow erosion notch around the right two-thirds. Sparse low Triassic vegetation and muted red-brown paleosol textures. Narrow horizon only in the top 15 percent. No river, pool, stream, wetland, or active eruption.

Subjects: exactly two dinosaurs total.
1) Exactly one Eoraptor lunensis in the lower-right middle ground, only about 18–22 percent of image width, walking calmly toward the right in a three-quarter rear view, not a broadside hero pose. Full animal visible with uncut tail, both hind feet clearly separated, both small forelimbs visible and not touching the ground. Compact basal sauropodomorph build, low skull, moderately long neck but never swan-necked, robust torso, short forelimbs; five-fingered hands with outer digits reduced rather than three equally dominant fingers.
2) Exactly one Chromogisaurus novasi far away on a stable upper-right shelf, only about 5–7 percent of image height, a clean separated silhouette moving in the same general direction but not looking at Eoraptor. Keep it distant because skull, neck, and hand details are poorly constrained; show only a modest slender basal sauropodomorph silhouette with a continuous uncut tail and two separated hind limbs.

Style/medium: naturalistic museum-grade paleoart, realistic but not cinematic spectacle, clear educational readability, original project-safe imagery.
Composition/framing: 16:9 landscape, low lateral raking camera looking along the eroded bankface. The geology is the primary subject and the two animals form a right-side two-step discovery path. Keep broad negative space across the left bank and ash ribbon. No centered animal, no S-curve river, no diagonal chase axis, no opposing face-off, no top-down view.
Lighting/mood: calm soft late-afternoon side light that reveals sediment layers; neutral atmospheric depth; no disaster mood.
Color palette: weathered ochre, muted terracotta, pale gray ash ribbon, restrained sage plants; natural animal colors consistent with the references but not copied pixel-for-pixel.
Constraints: exact animal count two; one Eoraptor and one distant Chromogisaurus; all limbs anatomically connected; no extra, fused, hidden, or amputated limbs; no split or cropped tails; no footprints; no carcass; no blood; no text; no labels; no border; no watermark.
Evidence boundary: The member-level setting and altered-ash layers are evidence-based, but the exact exposed bank shape, two animals being alive together, their positions, colors, behavior, weather, and moment are reconstructed. Do not imply that either animal witnessed an eruption or occupied the exact same ash bed or day.
Avoid: visible volcano or crater, eruption, falling ash, smoke plume, lava, panic, fleeing, chase, attack, herd or pack behavior, animals looking at each other, additional animals, eggs, nests, bones, modern grass, flowers, mammals, birds, broadside lineup, giant central dinosaur, raptor sickle claws, bird beaks, theropod monster heads, Plateosaurus-heavy bulk, quadrupedal lizard sprawl.
prompts.correction:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Input images: Image 1 is the edit target and current Dino Atlas ecosystem candidate.
Primary request: Change only the exposed pale altered-ash/bentonite layer and the narrow erosion separation near the right side so the old geological layer looks naturally weathered, thin, discontinuous, and lower-contrast instead of a continuous painted white stripe.

Required edit:
- Replace the current nearly continuous bright-white horizontal line with several irregular thin pale gray-to-buff bentonite lenses embedded in the same bankface.
- Keep the layer at approximately the same middle height, but break it naturally in at least three places with weathered sediment, small slumps, and erosion.
- Make the most important break near the right two-thirds a deeper shadowed erosion notch that visually separates the lower foreground surface from the distant upper-right shelf, without turning it into a river or canyon.
- The layer must read as an old exposed and altered deposit, never fresh falling ash, paint, a road marking, or a perfectly precise time line.

Critical invariants:
- Preserve the exact 16:9 framing, low lateral raking camera, overall bankface geometry, horizon, lighting, vegetation, color balance, and broad negative space.
- Preserve exactly the same two dinosaurs only: the lower-right Eoraptor and the distant upper-right Chromogisaurus.
- Do not add, remove, resize, move, restyle, blur, or anatomically alter either dinosaur. Keep every existing head, neck, body, both forelimbs, both hind limbs, feet, and each single continuous tail unchanged.
- Keep both animals facing generally right, separated in depth, not looking at or interacting with each other.
- No extra animals, footprints, bones, water, smoke, volcano, falling ash, fire, text, labels, borders, or watermark.
- This is an educational composite scene; do not add any visual cue implying simultaneous eruption, panic, chase, herd, or a shared exact bed.

evidence.supportedClaim: Both named taxa are documented from the Cancha de Bochas Member, and the member contains documented altered volcanic-ash or tuffaceous stratigraphic horizons. No shared fossil bed or direct association between the two taxa is established.
evidence.claimBoundary: The weathered band is a generalized older lithified tuffaceous or ash-bearing horizon exposed by erosion, not an active eruption, falling ash, or proof that either taxon occurs on that exact bed. The combined frame is a same-member stratigraphic comparison and does not claim the same moment, locality, encounter, interaction, ancestor-descendant relation, or shared response. Exact outcrop shape, band thickness, color and continuity, erosional relief, animal positions, simultaneous life appearance, weather and vegetation are reconstructed.

anatomy.verdict: Independent original-size review found exactly one Eoraptor and one Chromogisaurus. Each reads with one head, paired forelimbs, paired hind limbs and one continuous tail; no extra, fused, missing or cropped limbs or split tails are visible. Eoraptor hand and foot digits and all distant Chromogisaurus head, hand and foot details remain non-diagnostic.

ecology.verdict: Independent review accepted the corrected lower-contrast weathered layer only when the public card states that the taxa are a same-member comparison, not a shared bed, outcrop, moment or encounter, and that the exposed band is old altered material rather than an active eruption.

composition.verdict: Independent comparison against all 13 published scenes found a new geology-led lateral-section family: a left-dominant bankface, interrupted near-horizontal lenses and a same-direction lower-right/upper-right two-step discovery path.

contentSafety.verdict: Exactly two calm separated animals are visible with no contact, pursuit, panic, eruption, smoke, falling ash, injury, blood, carcass, text or watermark; independent review found the scene suitable for ages 5–14.
